title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 4. Pastimes at Sri Advaita's House
html:
The devotees of Navadvipa lament the Lord's sannyasa; Nityananda brings Shachi and the Vaishnavas to Advaita's house; the Lord comes there and spends a day and a night with them in kirtana, takes leave of Haridasa, Advaita and Gopinatha Acharya, and departs for Purushottama

Verse 1

आचार्यरत्नाद्धि निशम्य तद्वचो
हरेर्गुणास्वादविभिन्नधैर्याः।
आर्तस्वरैर्वा रुरुदुः सुदुःखिता
अद्वैतमुख्या द्विजसज्जनास्ततः॥१॥

ācāryaratnāddhi niśamya tadvaco
harerguṇāsvādavibhinnadhairyāḥ|
ārtasvarairvā ruruduḥ suduḥkhitā
advaitamukhyā dvijasajjanāstataḥ||1||

acharyaratnat — from the Acharyaratna; hi — indeed; nishamya — hearing; tat — that; vachah — account; hareh — of Hari; guna-asvada-vibhinna-dhairyah — their composure shattered by relishing (the tale of His) qualities; arta-svaraih — with cries of anguish; va — as it were; ruruduh — wept; su-duhkhitah — deeply grieved; advaita-mukhyah — headed by Advaita; dvija-sajjanah — the virtuous brahmanas; tatah — then.

1Hearing this account from the Acharyaratna, the virtuous brahmanas headed by Advaita lost their composure as they relished the tale of Hari's virtues, and, deeply grieved, they wept aloud as if in pain.

Verse 2

अथ श्रीजगदीशो हि भक्तानामार्तिनाशकः।
अद्वैताचार्यनिलये गच्छामीति मनो दधे॥२॥

atha śrījagadīśo hi bhaktānāmārtināśakaḥ|
advaitācāryanilaye gacchāmīti mano dadhe||2||

atha — now; shri-jagadishah — the Lord of the world; hi — indeed; bhaktanam — of the devotees; arti-nashakah — the dispeller of distress; advaita-acharya-nilaye — to the abode of Advaita Acharya; gachchhami — I shall go; iti — thus; manah dadhe — resolved.

2And the Lord of the world, who dispels the distress of His devotees, resolved, "I shall go to the abode of Advaita Acharya."

Verse 3

परिव्रज्य राढदेशं लोकैकनयनोत्सवः।
अवधूतं महात्मानं प्रोवाच मधुरं वचः॥३॥

parivrajya rāḍhadeśaṁ lokaikanayanotsavaḥ|
avadhūtaṁ mahātmānaṁ provāca madhuraṁ vacaḥ||3||

parivrajya — having wandered through; radha-desham — the Radha country; loka-eka-nayana-utsavah — the one festival for the eyes of the people; avadhutam — to the Avadhuta; maha-atmanam — the great soul; provacha — spoke; madhuram — sweet; vachah — words.

3Having wandered through the Radha country, He who is the one festival for the eyes of the people spoke sweetly to the great soul, the Avadhuta:

Verse 4

गच्छ त्वं जाह्नवीतीरे नवद्वीपं मनोरमम्।
मातरं परया भक्त्या मम नामपुरःसरम्॥४॥

gaccha tvaṁ jāhnavītīre navadvīpaṁ manoramam|
mātaraṁ parayā bhaktyā mama nāmapuraḥsaram||4||

gachchha — go; tvam — you; jahnavi-tire — on the bank of the Jahnavi; navadvipam — to Navadvipa; manoramam — the charming; mataram — mother; paraya — with the highest; bhaktya — devotion; mama — My; nama-purahsaram — with mention of the name.

4"Go to charming Navadvipa on the bank of the Jahnavi. With the highest devotion, in My name,

Verse 5

संशान्तय्य सुखीकृत्वा श्रीकृष्णचरितादिना।
तत्रत्यान्वैष्णवान्सर्वाञ्छ्रीवासादीन्मम प्रियान्॥५॥

saṁśāntayya sukhīkṛtvā śrīkṛṣṇacaritādinā|
tatratyānvaiṣṇavānsarvāñchrīvāsādīnmama priyān||5||

samshantayya — having calmed; sukhi-kritva — having comforted; shri-krishna-charita-adina — with the deeds of Sri Krishna and the like; tatratyan — who live there; vaishnavan — the Vaishnavas; sarvan — all; shrivasa-adin — Srivasa and the rest; mama — to Me; priyan — dear.

5calm and comfort My mother with tales of Sri Krishna's deeds and the like; and all the Vaishnavas there who are dear to Me, Srivasa and the rest,

Verse 6

समानयाचार्यगेहं यावत्तत्र व्रजाम्यहम्।
श्रुत्वाज्ञां जगदीशस्य जगाम त्वरया मुदा॥६॥

samānayācāryagehaṁ yāvattatra vrajāmyaham|
śrutvājñāṁ jagadīśasya jagāma tvarayā mudā||6||

samanaya — bring; acharya-geham — to the house of the Acharya; yavat — while; tatra — there; vrajami — am going; aham — I; shrutva — hearing; ajnam — the command; jagadishasya — of the Lord of the world; jagama — went; tvaraya — in haste; muda — with joy.

6bring to the Acharya's house, while I go there Myself." Hearing the command of the Lord of the world, Nityananda set out in haste and with joy

Verse 7

नवद्वीपं श्रिया युक्तं श्रीवासस्याश्रमं शुभम्।
विज्ञाप्य केशवाज्ञां स श्रीवासादिभिरन्वितः॥७॥

navadvīpaṁ śriyā yuktaṁ śrīvāsasyāśramaṁ śubham|
vijñāpya keśavājñāṁ sa śrīvāsādibhiranvitaḥ||7||

navadvipam — to Navadvipa; shriya — with splendour; yuktam — endowed; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; ashramam — to the dwelling; shubham — auspicious; vijnapya — announcing; keshava-ajnam — the command of Keshava; sah — he; shrivasa-adibhih — by Srivasa and the others; anvitah — accompanied.

7for Navadvipa, rich in splendour, to the auspicious dwelling of Srivasa. There He announced the command of Keshava1, and then the compassionate Nityananda, together with Srivasa and the others,

Verse 8

श्रीशचीचरणद्वन्द्वं नमस्कृत्य कृताञ्जलिः।
सान्त्वयित्वा च तां भक्त्या नित्यानन्दो दयानिधिः॥८॥

śrīśacīcaraṇadvandvaṁ namaskṛtya kṛtāñjaliḥ|
sāntvayitvā ca tāṁ bhaktyā nityānando dayānidhiḥ||8||

shri-shachi-charana-dvandvam — to the two feet of Sri Shachi; namaskritya — bowing; krita-anjalih — with joined palms; santvayitva — consoling; cha — and; tam — her; bhaktya — with devotion; nityanandah — Nityananda; daya-nidhih — the treasure-house of compassion.

8bowed with joined palms to the feet of Sri Shachi and consoled her with devotion.

Verse 9

तया पाचितमन्नं च भुक्त्वा स्थित्वा परे दिने।
सर्वैस्तैर्ब्राह्मणैः शूद्रैर्वैद्यैरपि महामनाः॥९॥

tayā pācitamannaṁ ca bhuktvā sthitvā pare dine|
sarvaistairbrāhmaṇaiḥ śūdrairvaidyairapi mahāmanāḥ||9||

taya — by her; pachitam — cooked; annam — the food; cha — and; bhuktva — having eaten; sthitva — having stayed (the night); pare — on the next; dine — day; sarvaih — with all; taih — those; brahmanaih — brahmanas; shudraih — shudras; vaidyaih — vaidyas; api — too; maha-manah — the magnanimous one.

9He ate the food she had cooked and stayed the night, and on the next day the magnanimous Nityananda, with all of them — brahmanas, shudras and vaidyas —

Verse 10

जगामाद्वैतनिलयं सहर्षस्त्वरयान्वितः।
शची च परया प्रीत्या पुत्रं श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम्॥१०॥

jagāmādvaitanilayaṁ saharṣastvarayānvitaḥ|
śacī ca parayā prītyā putraṁ śrīpuruṣottamam||10||

jagama — went; advaita-nilayam — to the abode of Advaita; sa-harshah — joyful; tvaraya anvitah — in haste; shachi — Shachi; cha — and; paraya — with the highest; pritya — love; putram — the son; shri-purushottamam — Sri Purushottama.

10hurried joyfully to the abode of Advaita. Shachi too hastened to the same place, to Advaita's house, thinking with the highest love of her son, Sri Purushottama.

Verse 11

मत्वा जगाम तत्रैव गेहेऽद्वैतस्य सत्वरा।
सर्वे ते तद्दिनं स्थित्वा भुक्त्वान्नं पावनं महत्॥११॥

matvā jagāma tatraiva gehe'dvaitasya satvarā|
sarve te taddinaṁ sthitvā bhuktvānnaṁ pāvanaṁ mahat||11||

matva — thinking (of her son as Purushottama); jagama — went; tatra eva — to that very place; gehe — to the house; advaitasya — of Advaita; satvara — in haste; sarve — all; te — they; tat-dinam — that day; sthitva — staying; bhuktva — having eaten; annam — the food; pavanam — purifying; mahat — great.

11All of them stayed there that day and partook of the great, purifying food

Verse 12

श्रीयुताद्वैतवर्यस्य शिवांशस्य महात्मनः।
ततः परदिने पुष्पग्रामादागच्छति प्रभौ॥१२॥

śrīyutādvaitavaryasya śivāṁśasya mahātmanaḥ|
tataḥ paradine puṣpagrāmādāgacchati prabhau||12||

shri-yuta-advaita-varyasya — of the venerable, excellent Advaita; shiva-amshasya — a portion of Shiva; maha-atmanah — the great soul; tatah — then; para-dine — on the next day; pushpa-gramat — from Pushpagrama; agachchhati — as (He) was coming; prabhau — the Lord.

12of the venerable Advaita, that great soul, a portion of Shiva2. And on the next day, as the Lord was coming from Pushpagrama3,

Verse 13

सर्वे ते मुदिता जग्मुस्तन्मङ्गलमहोत्सवाः।
अश्रुकम्पपुलकाद्यैः पूर्णाः परमविह्वलाः॥१३॥

sarve te muditā jagmustanmaṅgalamahotsavāḥ|
aśrukampapulakādyaiḥ pūrṇāḥ paramavihvalāḥ||13||

sarve — all; te — they; muditah — joyful; jagmuh — went (to meet Him); tat-mangala-maha-utsavah — for whom that was a great auspicious festival; ashru-kampa-pulaka-adyaih — with tears, trembling, thrills of rapture and the rest; purnah — filled; parama-vihvalah — utterly overwhelmed.

13they all went out joyfully to meet Him: for them it was a great and auspicious festival. Filled with tears, trembling and thrills of rapture, they were beside themselves.

Verse 14

तप्तकाञ्चनवपुर्धृतदण्डो
रक्तवस्त्रपरिवेष्टितदेहः।
मेरुशृङ्ग इव गैरिकयुक्त-
स्तेजसा हरिरिव प्रचकाशे॥१४॥

taptakāñcanavapurdhṛtadaṇḍo
raktavastrapariveṣṭitadehaḥ|
meruśṛṅga iva gairikayukta-
stejasā haririva pracakāśe||14||

tapta-kanchana-vapuh — His body like molten gold; dhrita-dandah — holding the staff; rakta-vastra-pariveshtita-dehah — His body wrapped in red cloth; meru-shringah — a peak of Meru; iva — like; gairika-yuktah — streaked with red ochre; tejasa — in radiance; harih — the sun; iva — like; prachakashe — He shone.

14His body was like molten gold, a staff was in His hand, and His frame was wrapped in red cloth: like a peak of Meru streaked with red ochre, He shone like the sun.

Verse 15

तं विलोक्य नृहरिं हरिदासाः
प्राणमात्मन इवाशु प्रणेमुः।
दण्डवद्भुवि निपत्य महान्तः
कान्तवक्त्रकमलं मुमुदुश्च॥१५॥

taṁ vilokya nṛhariṁ haridāsāḥ
prāṇamātmana ivāśu praṇemuḥ|
daṇḍavadbhuvi nipatya mahāntaḥ
kāntavaktrakamalaṁ mumuduśca||15||

tam — Him; vilokya — seeing; nriharim — Nrihari; hari-dasah — the servants of Hari; pranam — to the life-breath; atmanah — their own; iva — as if; ashu — at once; pranemuh — bowed down; danda-vat — like a staff; bhuvi — on the ground; nipatya — falling; mahantah — the great souls; kanta-vaktra-kamalam — (at) the lovely lotus face; mumuduh — rejoiced; cha — and.

15Seeing Nrihari, the servants of Hari at once bowed down to Him as if to their own breath of life; the great souls fell to the ground like staffs and rejoiced at the sight of His lovely lotus face.

Verse 16

नेत्रवारिझरपूरितदेहा
हर्षगद्गदरवाः पुलकाङ्गाः।
तान्विलोक्य भगवान्कृपाम्बुधि-
र्दृष्टिवृष्टिभिरलङ्कृतदेहान्॥१६॥

netravārijharapūritadehā
harṣagadgadaravāḥ pulakāṅgāḥ|
tānvilokya bhagavānkṛpāmbudhi-
rdṛṣṭivṛṣṭibhiralaṅkṛtadehān||16||

netra-vari-jhara-purita-dehah — their bodies bathed in streams of tears; harsha-gadgada-ravah — their voices choked with joy; pulaka-angah — their limbs thrilling; tan — them; vilokya — looking upon; bhagavan — Bhagavan; kripa-ambudhih — the ocean of mercy; drishti-vrishtibhih — with showers of glances; alankrita-dehan — their bodies adorned.

16Their bodies were bathed in streams of tears, their voices choked with joy, their limbs thrilled. Bhagavan, the ocean of mercy, looked upon them, and the shower of His glances adorned them.

Verse 17

स्पर्शनेन मुदितान्हसितेन
भाषितेन दृढहस्तग्रहेण।
पूर्णकामविभवान्स्मितकान्त-
दिव्यपद्मवदनः स हि चक्रे॥१७॥

sparśanena muditānhasitena
bhāṣitena dṛḍhahastagraheṇa|
pūrṇakāmavibhavānsmitakānta-
divyapadmavadanaḥ sa hi cakre||17||

sparshanena — by touch; muditan — delighted; hasitena — by laughter; bhashitena — by speech; dridha-hasta-grahena — by a firm clasp of the hand; purna-kama-vibhavan — rich in fulfilled desires; smita-kanta-divya-padma-vadanah — His divine lotus face lovely with a smile; sah — He; hi — indeed; chakre — made.

17By His touch, His smile, His words and the firm clasp of His hand, He whose divine lotus face was lovely with a smile delighted them and fulfilled all their desires.

Verse 18

तेऽपि हृष्टमनसः पुलकेन
पूरिताङ्गविभवाः सुखमीयुः।
तैः सुरेश इव देवसमूहै-
रागतः स भगवान्सहसैव॥१८॥

te'pi hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pulakena
pūritāṅgavibhavāḥ sukhamīyuḥ|
taiḥ sureśa iva devasamūhai-
rāgataḥ sa bhagavānsahasaiva||18||

te — they; api — too; hrishta-manasah — glad at heart; pulakena — with thrills of rapture; purita-anga-vibhavah — the splendour of their bodies brimming; sukham iyuh — attained happiness; taih — with them; sura-ishah — the lord of the gods; iva — like; deva-samuhaih — with hosts of gods; agatah — came; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sahasa eva — straightway.

18And they, glad at heart, the splendour of their bodies brimming with thrills of rapture, attained happiness. With them, like the lord of the gods with the hosts of the gods, Bhagavan came straightway

Verse 19

अद्वितीयगुरुवर्यनिकेतं
रोचयन्स नितरां पदपद्मैः।
आसने समुपविश्य सुक्लृप्ते
राजमान इव तिग्मदीधितिः॥१९॥

advitīyaguruvaryaniketaṁ
rocayansa nitarāṁ padapadmaiḥ|
āsane samupaviśya suklṛpte
rājamāna iva tigmadīdhitiḥ||19||

advitiya-guru-varya-niketam — the dwelling of the peerless (Advaita), the most excellent guru; rochayan — illuminating; sah — He; nitaram — wholly; pada-padmaih — with His lotus feet; asane — on a seat; samupavishya — sitting down; su-klripte — well prepared; rajamanah — shining; iva — like; tigma-didhitih — the sun of fierce rays.

19and, wholly illuminating with His lotus feet the dwelling of the peerless4, most excellent guru, sat down on the seat prepared for Him and shone like the sun of fierce rays.

Verse 20

सञ्जगौ हरिकथां सगद्गदं
नेत्रवारिभिरलङ्कृतदेहः।
बदरिकाश्रम इव ऋषिमध्ये
राजति स्म स नारायणदेवः॥२०॥

sañjagau harikathāṁ sagadgadaṁ
netravāribhiralaṅkṛtadehaḥ|
badarikāśrama iva ṛṣimadhye
rājati sma sa nārāyaṇadevaḥ||20||

sanjagau — sang; hari-katham — the story of Hari; sa-gadgadam — in a faltering voice; netra-varibhih — with tears; alankrita-dehah — His body adorned; badarika-ashrame — at Badarikashrama; iva — as; rishi-madhye — amid the sages; rajati sma — shone; sah — He; narayana-devah — the god Narayana.

20In a faltering voice He sang the story of Hari; His body was adorned with tears, and He shone like the god Narayana amid the sages at Badarikashrama5.

Verse 21

श्रीशचीं प्रणिपत्याह सादरं करुणामयः।
तिष्ठामि सततं मातस्तव सन्निहितो ह्यहम्॥२१॥

śrīśacīṁ praṇipatyāha sādaraṁ karuṇāmayaḥ|
tiṣṭhāmi satataṁ mātastava sannihito hyaham||21||

shri-shachim — to Sri Shachi; pranipatya — bowing down; aha — said; sa-adaram — respectfully; karuna-mayah — the compassionate one; tishthami — I abide; satatam — always; matah — O mother; tava — you; sannihitah — near; hi — surely; aham — I.

21The compassionate one bowed respectfully to Sri Shachi and said, "Mother, I am always near you."

Verse 22

अद्वैताचार्यवर्येण दत्तमन्नं चतुर्विधम्।
बुभुजे यज्ञभुङ्नाथो भक्तैर्भक्तजनेष्टदः॥२२॥

advaitācāryavaryeṇa dattamannaṁ caturvidham|
bubhuje yajñabhuṅnātho bhaktairbhaktajaneṣṭadaḥ||22||

advaita-acharya-varyena — by the excellent Advaita Acharya; dattam — offered; annam — food; chatuh-vidham — of four kinds; bubhuje — ate; yajna-bhuk-nathah — the Lord who enjoys the sacrifices; bhaktaih — with the devotees; bhakta-jana-ishta-dah — granting the desires of His devotees.

22The Lord who enjoys the sacrifices, who grants His devotees their desires, ate together with the devotees the four kinds of food6 offered by the excellent Advaita Acharya.

Verse 23

तत्र सुप्तो रजन्यां स शेषे यामे समुत्थितः।
गायन्कलपदं कृष्णं ननर्त स्वजनैः सह॥२३॥

tatra supto rajanyāṁ sa śeṣe yāme samutthitaḥ|
gāyankalapadaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ nanarta svajanaiḥ saha||23||

tatra — there; suptah — having slept; rajanyam — at night; sah — He; sheshe — in the last; yame — watch; samutthitah — rising; gayan — singing of; kala-padam — sweetly; krishnam — Krishna; nanarta — danced; sva-janaih saha — with His own.

23He slept there that night, and in the last watch He rose and, sweetly singing of Krishna, danced with His own.

Verse 24

अथ प्रभाते विमले श्रीवासादीन्द्विजोत्तमान्।
वाचा मधुरयोवाच गच्छत स्वाश्रमान्प्रति॥२४॥

atha prabhāte vimale śrīvāsādīndvijottamān|
vācā madhurayovāca gacchata svāśramānprati||24||

atha — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; shrivasa-adin — to Srivasa and the rest; dvija-uttaman — the best of brahmanas; vacha — in words; madhuraya — sweet; uvacha — said; gachchhata — go; sva-ashraman prati — to your homes.

24Then, in the clear dawn, He said sweetly to Srivasa and the other best of brahmanas, "Go to your homes.

Verse 25

यास्यामि देवदेवेशपुरुषोत्तमदर्शने।
सार्वभौमद्विजेन्द्रेण सार्धं पश्यामि तं हरिम्॥२५॥

yāsyāmi devadeveśapuruṣottamadarśane|
sārvabhaumadvijendreṇa sārdhaṁ paśyāmi taṁ harim||25||

yasyami — I shall go; deva-deva-isha-purushottama-darshane — to see Purushottama, the Lord of the god of gods; sarvabhauma-dvija-indrena — with Sarvabhauma, the king of brahmanas; sardham — together; pashyami — I shall see; tam — that; harim — Hari.

25I shall go to see Purushottama, the Lord of the god of gods; together with Sarvabhauma7, the king of brahmanas, I shall see that Hari.

Verse 26

युष्माभिरत्र कर्तव्यं सदैव हरिकीर्तनम्।

✦

Notes

  1. Keshava is here a name of the Lord (Krishna Chaitanya).
  2. "Portion" (amsha) does not diminish Advaita: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching He is Maha-Vishnu Himself, together with Sadashiva, non-different from the Lord (cf. 1.04, note to v. 5; 2.18, note to v. 29); "Shiva" here is Sadashiva, with whom Advaita is one.
  3. Pushpagrama ("Flower Village") — apparently Phuliya, a village near Shantipura.
  4. "Peerless" (advitiya, literally "without a second") — a play on the name Advaita ("Non-dual").
  5. At Badarikashrama in the Himalayas the god Narayana, in the form of a sage, performs austerities surrounded by the rishis.
  6. That is, food that is chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
  7. Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, a learned brahmana of Navadvipa who lived in Puri; the meeting with him is described in the following sargas.
  8. The day of Hari is Ekadashi, the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, kept with fasting and a night vigil.
  9. A blade of grass between the teeth is a sign of utter humility.
  10. Advaita wonders that He feels no pain of separation and asks whether it is the Lord who holds His love in check; the Lord replies that if it showed itself in full, He would be unable to leave.
  11. Gopinatha Acharya, a brahmana of Navadvipa who later met the Lord in Puri.
  12. In Haridasa Dasa's edition (witness C) this verse comes after the next one, which is more natural to the sense.
